Researchers report contrasting measurements

Researchers working at a coastal observation station published a new comparison of local measurements on Monday. The team said that a change in one season should not be treated as evidence of a permanent shift in the regional climate.

"Not yet."

Dr Elena Ruiz said the instruments recorded a temperature of 21.5 degrees Celsius, compared with 20.8 degrees a year earlier. The team did not claim that the measurements established a cause, and independent reviewers requested a longer record.

  • Check the instrument calibration.
  • Retain the original observation logs.

The comparison included two stations with different exposure to wind and sunlight. Their readings were evaluated separately before the researchers calculated the difference, rather than combining the figures into a single unexplained total.

"The result is preliminary," Ruiz said. The group plans to repeat the study after a complete annual cycle and publish the calibration history together with the raw measurements so that other researchers can inspect the comparison.
